|Geographer Mercator|
Oh $n, I was just looking for you.
Actually, I have a favor to ask of you.
A favor? Go ahead, I'll do whatever I can to help you out.
After all, it was your recommendation that got me my teaching job at the university.
Well then, listen up! Now I know that as a fellow geographer, you have an interest in the cartography of the world.
Oh, absolutely. The New World, the Middle East, Asia.
I'd love to travel the world and see for myself all the things I've read about in my studies.
But I don't have any money. And a professor's salary, well...
I suspected as much. Now, I too have longed to travel the world and discover new lands.
But I am old and weak, and though I'm ashamed to admit it, I hate ships.
But you're young and strong, with a thirst for knowledge and adventure. Am I right?
Oh yes! I can't say that teaching is very exciting. I'd like to live a life on the brink, full of unexpected surprises.
That's just what I thought! Now, how does this strike you?
I'll supply the money. How'd you like to make a career out of being an explorer?
Really?! Why, I can't think of anything that would make me happier.
So you'll go and explore the world in my place?
Well, what exactly do I need to do?
I need you to seek out the unknown, to explore the vast regions of the world.
As you travel to these far-off lands, you'll learn the most sought after knowledge of our time,
distant ports and uncharted waters.
So we can make maps for other sailors!
Exactly. My goal is to make a map with details of the whole entire world! No one's done that, yet!
A map of the whole world! That's a big job. We'll be competing with all the other adventurers, mapmakers, and scholars.
Correct. If we're going to do it, we've got to do it better and faster than anyone else.
This map could make us famous!
You can count on me, Mercator!
Alright then, here's the money I promised you.
There's a ship all ready to go, waiting for you at the docks.
You don't waste any time, do you? Have you already decided what to call the ship?
Not yet. I thought I'd leave that up to you.
Is that so? Well then, it's decided. I'll name it 'Mercator' in your honor, since you can't come with me.
Why thank you, $n. Oh, I almost forgot. I'd like to introduce you to someone. He's going to be traveling with you.
I figured you'd need a mate to teach you the ropes of sea travel, so I searched around for the best in seamen. His name is Hans.

|Sailor Hans Starten|
Ahoy there, Professor! I hear ye'll be needing an old sea dog like myself.
Hans's my name, pleased to meet ye.
I'm $n! We've got a long voyage ahead of us. I'm afraid it may be rough going at times.
Are you willing to join me on such a dangerous adventure?
Well, professor, a long time ago ye very own father helped me through a rough spot, and I've been in his debt ever since.
I'll do anything I can to help his son, Professor.
Thank you. But stop that professor stuff, I'm now officially retired!
Why don't you call me Captain, just like a real sea-faring crew.
Aye, then Captain it is, Professor!
But, oh, never mind. Well Mercator, thank you again, and we'll be heading off!
Don't forget to keep me updated on your progress! I hope you have a safe journey!
Mercator
Welcome, Professor $s. What can I do for you?
Please, everyone, stop calling me Professor! It's embarrassing.
Oh, your friend Mercator was in here looking for you, Professor.
Mercator? I wonder what he wants?
I don't know, but he said he'd be waiting at his shop.
Don't forget to keep me updated on your progress! Good luck! Have a safe journey!
Don't worry about a thing, Mercator. We're off!
Prof..I mean, Captain! Where will we go first?
Well, Hans, why not Northern Europe? Have you ever heard of the Fjords?
Aye, the Fjords of Norway. They were created when massive ice blocks slid off the mountains and carved the land below, right?
Aye, I've heard many a sailor tell of their majestic beauty.
Wow, you really know your stuff! The Fjords are a major reason why the coastline of Northern Europe is so jagged.
Aye, ye are a wise one, Prof... Cap'n. Ye know, I've always wanted to take a look at that coastline.
Me too! I'm tired of reading about things like the Fjords, I want to see them with my own eyes!
Aye, Cap'n, but it gets dangerous up north. If we were hit by some floating ice, we'd sink before you could say Kris Kringle.
So, until ye've had time to gather some experience, I don't think we should venture too far.
Especially so far North, since safe harbors there are few and far between.
We'd be a sad and sorry lot if we ran out of provisions at sea. Aye, that would be a fine mess!
You're very right, Hans. We'll have to watch our supplies carefully.
Although I'm grateful to him for this opportunity, Mercator sure didn't give us much gold. I'm afraid it won't get us very far.
Well, Cap'n, we'll just have to make do. And I bet we'll discover some rare things in our travels. Collectors will pay a heap of gold to know such things!
If we have a contract, we can trade information about the whereabouts for money.
That's a good idea, but do you really think we'll be able to discover those rare items?
Sure as my name is Hans, Cap'n! First of all, as we travel the world we're bound to find some villages.
We should disembark and form a search party. I'm sure we'll find something more often than not!
And if we don't find anything, we should entertain and befriend the villagers. They know the secrets of their land.
I've heard sailors say that a rare item can be found in every village! We'll discover lots if we just keep on looking!
Forget your worries about gold. We'll be rich as kings!
I'm lucky to have you, Hans. You know everything!
Far from it, Prof... I mean Captain. I learned all that from ye father, a very wise and good man.
My father? Really? It's my dream to be a better geographer than my father.
So $n, have you gotten used to sea travel yet?
$n, I 'd like to believe this is just a rumor but... is it true that you have contracts with other cartographers besides me?
It is true?! I can't believe you would go and betray me!
I want you to renew your contract with me.
Don't betray me again. It would mean the end of both our friendship and trust.
Captain $n, I heard talk around the port that Mercator's maps have been getting popular!
And I heard that both Mercator and you, $n, are listed as cartographers.
That's great! But we can't let our fame go to our heads. We'll have to work even harder from here on out.
Righto, Captain! Let's move her out to sea, men!
Oh, please, wait a minute! Can you please take me on your ship?
Huh? Are ye crazy, miss? There's no place for children on a ship. Get along home now, lassie.
Are you the Captain, mister? Please, let me aboard.
I'll prove my worth. I can speak any language in the world.
Why yes, I am the Captain. What's your name?
I'm Paula. Please let me aboard, Captain. I want to find my homeland.
Your homeland? What do you mean you're looking for your homeland? I want to hear about this.
And by the way, I'm $n $s, an adventurer traveling the globe to make a world map.
A world map... so, you mean, are you the famous $s of 'Mercator and $s'?
Yes. Well, if you don't mind, maybe you'd tell me why you want to board my ship.
I... a couple of days ago, my father died. Right before he died, he said to me, 'I have to tell you the truth. I'm not your real father.'
Ten years ago, he found me in the markets of Seville. I was only 4 years old, so he took me and raised me as his own.
My father, the man who raised me, was a trader, so he traveled all over the world.
He said that he searched for my real parents wherever he went.
But he never found them, and so I've been with him ever since.
'Your homeland, find your homeland...' Those were my father's last words.
I beg you. Please let me aboard. I swear I won't cause you any trouble.
But...
(Sniff) Professor, (Sniff) this old barnacle-back hasn't heard such a touching story in many a year! (Sniff)
What a brave young lassie! Going out alone to search for her homeland... I say we let her aboard.
But Hans, didn't you just say there was no room for... oh, well, come along then, miss.
Oh! Thank you!
So Captain $n, have you got your sea legs yet?
Hey $n! Huh? Who's the girl?
Nice to meet you. My name's Paula. You're Mercator, the famous cartographer, aren't you?
I love your maps! They're absolutely wonderful.
Why thank you, miss.
This young girl is all alone. She's joined our crew to travel the world in search of her homeland.
Oh, I see. Well, I hope you find your homeland, miss. Now, $n, how about some results from your travels?
$n, I want to believe this is just a rumor but... have you made contracts with other cartographers besides me?
Really?! I can't believe you would just turn around and stab me in the back like that!
Well, I'm going to have you renew your contract with me again.
But you had better not double-cross me again, or it'll mean the end of our friendship and trust.
Did you know that the reputation of Mercator's maps has sky-rocketed?
As well it should, lassie! They're the latest and most accurate.
Success really does wonders for a man! Let's go!
It doesn't look like this harbor is my homeland either...
Oh, missie, don't look so disappointed, it makes me heart ache. We'll find your home some day!
He's right. There are still so many places in the world we haven't been to yet.
You're right. Thank you, $n. Thank you, Hans.
Hans, the sea is really interesting, isn't it? The morning sea, the evening sea... I'm glad we decided to make this voyage.
The way the sea goes out forever... it's so romantic.
Aye missie, that's because ye've only seen a calm sea. The wrath of a stormy sea strikes fear in the heart of even the bravest sailor.
Welcome back, $n, Hans, Paula. The sea's treating you all fine, I see!
How about sharing some of the information you've gathered?
$n, I want to believe this is just a rumor but... have you made contracts with other cartographers besides me?
Really?! I can't believe you would just turn around and stab me in the back like that!
Well, I'm going to have you renew your contract with me again.
But you had better not double-cross me again, or it'll mean the end of our friendship and trust.
I heard that Mercator's atlas is being published internationally now.
Is that so? He ought to be getting a nice bit o' gold then.
He gets 20,000 gold pieces a month just from royalties!
Arrr, so when are we going to see some of that gold, I wonder?
Oh, forget about him. Who could put a price on all the fantastic things we've seen?
And I'd still be a professor if it wasn't for his help.
We haven't had much luck finding Paula's homeland, have we?
We've been to almost every harbor in the world.
I'm sorry I've caused you so much trouble.
Why, it's no trouble at all! But if we can, we just want to find it for you as quickly as possible.
Exactly. But even if we don't, ye needn't fret. The Captain here said that if he could, he'd like to stay with ye forever.
D..Don't say silly things like that! Paula will misunderstand.
$n, don't you think the sea is fantastic and mysterious?
That's because depending on the latitude and weather, it changes in form.
But, I wouldn't be too upset if I never see a stormy sea.
The emerald of the Mediterranean, the green of the Aegean Sea, the deep blue of the Indian Sea-
they're all so beautiful.
Ahhh, an old sea dog like meself just can't get excited about such things after so many years.
Oh, Hans, there must be something you dream about!
Oh $n, I take it you've brought me some new information.
$n, I want to believe this is just a rumor but... have you made contracts with other cartographers besides me?
Really?! I can't believe you would just turn around and stab me in the back like that!
Well, I'm going to have you renew your contract with me again.
But you had better not double-cross me again, or it'll mean the end of our friendship and trust.
Captain, as I'm getting on in me years, there's one wish I have, one dream I've kept in my heart for a long time, that I hope will come true.
What is it, Hans? If you don't mind, I'd like to hear it.
Well then, Cap'n, Paula, have you two heard about the golden country of Zipangu?
I read about Marco Polo and his voyage to the Far East. Is that the same Zipangu?
Aye, the same. I read Marco Polo's book when I was just a lad, and ever since I've wanted to go there and see it for meself.
The golden country of Zipangu? If it really exists, I'd like to go and add it to my map.
Why don't we go and have a look?
Have you heard the latest news about Mercator? Our maps have earned him election to the Royal Academy of Scholars.
Aye, he's one shrewd operator, Captain. I feel like he got rich and famous off of ye own hard efforts, Captain.
Aw, don't let it bother you. I enjoy making accurate maps and knowing that I am somehow helping out other seafarers.
By the way, don't you two think it's about time you took the oath?
Take the oath? What are you talking about?
Why your marriage of course! Your marriage oath!
Come on, cut it out now Hans. It's embarrassing!
Stop your joking now, Hans. You know we are not involved in that way. Right $n?
Well, if you say so...
... Whew.
We still haven't found Paula's homeland.
We've been to almost every port I can think of.
I'm sorry. I didn't mean to cause you so much trouble.
Stop your nonsense! No one here thinks of you as trouble. We just want to help you find your homeland, that's all.
Exactly. You don't have to worry about that. Besides, the Captain here said he'd kind of like it if you stayed on with us.
D..don't say such silly things, Hans. Paula will get the wrong idea.
Hmmm, you've really become quite the sailor, now haven't you.
Do you happen to have any new information to give to me?
$n, I want to believe this is just a rumor but... have you made contracts with other cartographers besides me?
Really?! I can't believe you would just turn around and stab me in the back like that!
Well, I'm going to have you renew your contract with me again.
But you had better not double-cross me again, or it'll mean the end of our friendship and trust.
By any chance, is this land... Zipangu?
No, it's most certainly not! Zipangu, I never heard of such a place!
No. Zipangu is farther to the northeast.
What? Zipangu is right around here? Captain, let's go!
So, $n, it looks like you still haven't found Paula's homeland yet.
I take it you have new information for me?
$n, I want to believe this is just a rumor but... have you made contracts with other cartographers besides me?
Really?! I can't believe you would just turn around and stab me in the back like that!
Well, I'm going to have you renew your contract with me again.
But you had better not double-cross me again, or it'll mean the end of our friendship and trust.
By any chance, is this land... Zipangu?
No, Zipangu is a little farther northeast.
What? We're almost there! Captain, let's go!
Why yes, to westerners our land of the rising sun is known as Zipangu.
I can't believe me ears, Cap'n! This is Zipangu! We made it!
Is this really the golden country?
It sure doesn't look like a golden country. Let's take a look around the port city.
You know, Hans, something has just occurred to me.
What is it, Cap'n?
Don't you think that the people here look a lot like Paula?
Aye, now that ye mention it, I do see a likeness.
So, you think this could be my homeland?
I don't know. Paula, I've refrained from asking this until now, but I want you to tell me everything you remember about yourself.
I think that we might be able to get something, a clue to help find your homeland.
I really don't remember anything at all. Not my parents, my home, nothing. It's all long forgotten.
Don't rush it, just slowly try to remember anything you can.
Like the landscape around ye home. Ye must remember something.
For instance, it was surrounded by mountains, or there was a large river...
I don't remember any mountains, or rivers, absolutely noth... wait a minute!
Yes, I remember, there was an ocean... an ocean, but strange. It wasn't blue.
Huh? It wasn't blue? What does that mean?
It was muddy. Yellowish... a yellow sea!
A yellow sea? Hans, have you ever heard of anything like that?
What foolishness are ye talking about? There's no such thing as a yellow sea!
Oh, but it's true, it's true! I remember it clearly now.
What Paula says is probably true. She's got no reason to lie.
Well, of course, I know that. But, a yellow sea?!
Well, at least we have a clue. Let's go see if anyone knows anything about a yellow sea.
Hey $n. Are you and Paula getting along OK?
I take it you have some new information for me.
$n, I want to believe this is just a rumor but... have you made contracts with other cartographers besides me?
Really?! I can't believe you would just turn around and stab me in the back like that!
Well, I'm going to have you renew your contract with me again.
But you had better not double-cross me again, or it'll mean the end of our friendship and trust.
Excuse me, I wonder if you might answer a question?
Yes, what is it?
Do you know anything about a yellow sea?
A yellow sea? Never heard of it.
If it's a yellow river you're looking for, though, that'd be the Huang He.
The Huang He?
Yes, it's a really wide river. The mouth of the river is at 37@N and 120@E.
So the only information we could get was about a yellow river.
Isn't this right around the mouth to that yellow river?
You may be right!
Wait a minute. That villager said that the Huang He was a wide river, right?
Yes, but what about it?
The yellow sea I remember was always flowing in the same direction!
And there was never a changing of the tides, and I don't think I ever smelled the salty brine of the sea.
So it was probably a river, not the sea... It was just so wide that it looked like a sea.
Well then, let's go to this yellow river and check things out.
Excuse me, I wonder if you might answer a question?
Yes, what is it?
Do you know anything about a yellow sea?
A yellow sea? Never heard of it.
If it's a yellow river you're looking for though, that'd be the Huang He.
Huang He?
Yes, it's a really wide river. The mouth of the river is at 37@N 120@E.
I take it you have some new information for me.

Well, I'm going to have you renew your contract with me again.
But you had better not double-cross me again, or it'll mean the end of our friendship and trust.
This building...
Paula, do you remember anything about this building?
Maybe, just maybe, this is her home!
I only remember vaguely, but I'm fairly certain...
Ah, you are Paula's...
